ui_bugs.issue: The input is prefilled from the project's postcode (demo project returns NG3 5AP, so sold-no-postcode never shows) but when a user focuses the field it does not select-all. Typing a new postcode without first clearing concatenates onto the existing text (e.g. 'NG3 5APNG7 1AA'), which trips backend max_length=10 and surfaces as 'String should have at most 10 characters' in sold-error. Repro: open /sold-map, tap Postcode, type 'NG7 1AA', tap Search.

When /sold-prices returns 422 (postcode exceeds max_length=10, or any Pydantic validation), the raw Pydantic detail is rendered inside sold-error. A friendlier guard client-side ('Enter a full UK postcode, e.g. NG7 1AA' before firing the query, or trimming/normalising the stored value) would avoid the cryptic 'String should have at most 10 characters'.

action_items: Minor UX: in sold-map.tsx select-all on focus for the postcode Field, or reset `input` to '' when the user taps the field so a fresh postcode doesn't get appended to the prefilled project value.
Minor UX: handle 422 responses from /sold-prices in sold-map.tsx with a friendly message (currently the raw Pydantic 'String should have at most 10 characters' is shown in sold-error).

Optional: the demo-project note in the request ('demo project may not have a postcode -> sold-no-postcode card') no longer matches reality - the demo project address contains NG3 5AP, so sold-no-postcode is unreachable through the demo user. If you want to exercise that branch in testing, add a project without a postcode in the address.

routes/sold_prices.py: median/avg exclude type == 'Other' (commercial/bulk sales) which prevents skewed averages, this is correctly surfaced in the UI muted note.
routes/sold_prices.py: cache key = `{pc}|{years}|{miles}` with 24h TTL via sold_price_cache collection; second call for the same key is sub-second (verified).

sold-map.tsx: good testID coverage (sold-map-screen, sold-controls, sold-postcode-input, sold-search-button, sold-miles-*, sold-years-*, sold-loading, sold-map, sold-stats, sold-median/avg/count, sold-gdv-compare, sold-type-all/{Type}, sold-list, sold-sale-{i}, sold-show-more, sold-error, sold-retry, sold-no-postcode, sold-empty, sold-back-button).

rca_of_issue: Field prefill behaviour: const projectPc = p?.address.match(PC_RE)?.[1]?.toUpperCase() ?? ''; const [input, setInput] = useState<string | null>(null); and Field value={input ?? pc}. Because `input` starts null, the Field shows `pc` (the project postcode), but the underlying TextInput value is still the prefilled string. React Native Web does not select-all on focus by default, so any typed chars are appended. Fix is either (a) set the initial `input` state to projectPc so the TextInput value is user-owned from the start and selectTextOnFocus works, or (b) wire `selectTextOnFocus` + `onFocus={() => setInput('')}` on the Field.
